payload.seo_title: AI Wedding Vows and How to Make Them Sound Like You
payload.meta_description: Use AI wedding vows as a drafting partner, not a ghostwriter. A prompt built from your own stories, edits that cut clichés and the legal words to keep.
secondary_keywords: using ai to write wedding vows

audience.notes: Busy 30s professionals (persona: senior lawyer and finance), planning abroad. They will use AI for speed but fear ending up with something generic (persona fear 3) and do not want to be the Reddit story. Planning from far away (fear 2) means they rarely meet the celebrant in person before the day.

payload.search_intent: Informational with a how-to core: 'can I, should I, and how do I use AI for my vows without it sounding like AI?'. The SERP also carries a strong reassurance intent driven by backlash stories.
payload.angle: AI as a drafting partner, not a ghostwriter. You bring the stories, AI brings structure, you edit out the AI. Covers a prompt framework built from your own stories, editing out generic phrasing, a read-aloud length check, a before and after example written by us, the legal words AI cannot change, and privacy.
serp_gaps_to_win: Legal words: no top-3 result says AI-drafted vows sit after the Marriage Act s45(2) words in Australia, or that abroad the local registrar or embassy decides.
Before and after edit: nobody shows a generic AI draft turned into a specific one.
Privacy: nobody covers what not to paste into a chatbot.
Backlash answered practically: tell your partner, write the raw material yourself, agree length and tone first.

outline.h2: Can AI write your wedding vows?
outline.answers: Yes, it can draft them, but the words that land are the ones only you know. Snippet answer in 40 to 55 words for the AI Overview and PAA 'Can AI write wedding vows?'.
must_include: The backlash in one line (couples on Reddit reacting badly to AI-written vows), no quotes or links to Reddit
Practical rule: agree with your partner whether either of you will use AI, so nobody is surprised
Name ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini once as examples of general assistants, no ranking, no pricing

outline.h2: Write your own raw material before you open a chat
outline.answers: Why the first draft has to come from you, and how to get it in ten minutes.
must_include: Link /how-to-write-wedding-vows for the five questions (do not reproduce all five; summarise and link)
Voice memo or bullet notes: three specific memories, one habit, two to four promises

outline.h2: A prompt that keeps your vows sounding like you
must_include: Prompt template in a code or quote block: role (editor, not author), your notes pasted in, target about 150 words, your tone, banned words list, 'ask me questions before you write', 'keep my phrases where you can'
Ask for structure options, not a finished vow

outline.h2: Edit out what sounds like AI
outline.answers: How to spot and cut generic lines, and answer PAA 'What to avoid when writing vows?'.
must_include: Stranger test from our parent guide (if a stranger could say it about their partner, cut it), linked
A short list of tell-tale phrases to cut (e.g. soulmate, journey, tapestry, endless devotion, partner in crime)
Before and after example written by us: one generic AI-style paragraph, then the edited version with one real detail and plain promises. Must be original
One line on 'I vow' vs 'I promise' (PAA): either works; 'I will' and 'I promise' beat 'I'll try'

outline.h2: Check the length aloud and keep the legal words
outline.answers: The invisible work: timing, the legal wording, and what changes abroad.
must_include: Length per our live parent page: about 150 words, about a minute aloud, 300 words the most we suggest (NOT the link map's old '250 to 300 words' note)
Australia: personal vows follow the Marriage Act 1961 s45(2) words, which AI must not rewrite; link the Attorney-General's Department or legislation.gov.au at the claim
Abroad: the local registrar or embassy decides what is legal; an Australian celebrant cannot perform a legal marriage overseas (AGD), so a ceremony they lead abroad is symbolic
Send the final vow to your celebrant early; print it on a card, not your phone

outline.h2: What not to share with an AI chatbot
must_include: Advice only: skip full names, health details, family conflict and anything your partner would not want stored; check the tool's data or history settings
Cite OAIC only if a page speaks to individuals using AI chatbots; otherwise keep it as our advice, no legal claim

outline.h2: Where Wonderland Studio's AI Planning Assistant fits
outline.answers: Use a general assistant for the words; use Studio for the planning around them.
must_include: Describe the assistant ONLY with live /wonderland-studio wording: 'Ask your AI Planning Assistant. Timing, budgets, destinations, etiquette. Ask anything, any hour.'
Do NOT say it writes vows: our live comparison page says 'It's not a writing studio: for vows, toasts, thank-you notes and long emails, ChatGPT or another general assistant is the better tool.'
Do NOT state its price or trial: SITE-CONFLICT (see open_questions)
Link /expert-advice/chatgpt-vs-ai-wedding-planner as the AI cluster head
One line on Wedded Concierge arranging venue, sound and running order with your celebrant abroad (wording from /how-to-write-wedding-vows)

faqs: Is it wrong to use AI to write your wedding vows?

must_include: Persona fear 3 (spending a lot and still getting something generic): the whole edit section and the before and after example answer it; say plainly that a generator's first draft is generic by design.
Persona fear 2 (planning from the other side of the world): legal-words and abroad notes, send vows to the celebrant early, Concierge handles sound and running order.
Official sources linked at the claim: AGD or legislation.gov.au for s45(2) and celebrants abroad.
Before and after example written by us, original.

Claiming Studio's AI Planning Assistant writes or edits vows
